data: All Quality Control Requirements must be performed and pass the applicable acceptance criteria, before any sample analysis. Any analytes that do not meet all criteria must be re-injected in the same or different sequence for those analytes that contain reportable results for any sample(s) assayed. Sequences may be stopped early, and restarted, to address any issues relating to Quality Control.

CCV is injected a minimum of three times at the start of the run. The last three injections must have an accuracy of ±15% of the nominal concentration (20 ppm) and %RSD <= 5% for each cannabinoid before continuing the run.

To demonstrate accuracy and precision, the CCV is injected a minimum of three times. The last three injections must have an accuracy of ±10% of the nominal concentration (20 ppm) for each cannabinoid. The precision of the last three injections must have an %RSD ≤5% (using sample standard deviation) for all cannabinoids.
There are no interfering peaks or carryover present in the blank injections
The resolution between every cannabinoid in the CCV injections should be ≥1.0.
The LOQ must have an accuracy of ±20% for each cannabinoid.

If a calibration curve is run, the back calculated concentration at each level must ±10% of the nominal concentration for each cannabinoid. The coefficient of determination (r2) must be ≥0.99 for all cannabinoids.
The LCS injections are 80-120% of the nominal concentration for each cannabinoid before samples are analyzed
Inject ACN as a reagent blank. The blank injection must be free of any interfering peaks and/or background contamination.
Each cannabinoid in the calibration curve is within ±10% of the nominal at each level
The LOQ should have an accuracy of ±10% for each cannabinoid.
The r2 is ≥0.99 for each cannabinoid calibration curve

Laboratory Control Samples have an acceptance criterion of the ±20% nominal concentration for each cannabinoid. LCSs outside of the ±20% should be reprepared/extracted along with any concurrently prepared samples of the same matrix type if it is determined that the HPLC is not at fault. Only the non-carboxylic acid moieties of the cannabinoids in the scope of this SOP will be analyzed in Beverage and Edible Laboratory Control Samples.
The Rs is ≥1.0 between the d9-THC and d8-THC peaks

One sample duplicate must be prepped every 20 samples. Duplicate samples can be from any of the matrices described above. Duplicate LCSs may be used as well. The reportable results (concentration) for each Duplicate must have a %Difference of ≤±10% (Equation 1) for each analyte. 

If samples are prepped in
duplicate, then the reportable results of the first sample injected will be
used.
A duplicate sample is prepped every 20 samples. Each duplicate must be a ≤±20% difference compared to the original sample ran
The LOQ must have an accuracy of ±20% for each cannabinoid
CCV injections must bracket every 10 sample and LCS injections. The accuracy of each CCV injection must be of ±10% of the nominal concentration for each cannabinoid.
CCV injections must bracket every 10 sample and LCS injections and each cannabinoid is within ±15% of the nominal concentration
Process the batch run results using quadratic regression with 1/C2 weighting at 220 nm in LabSolutions.
Manual peak identification and integration are permitted if it is apparent relevant peaks are not properly processed by the software.

A sample is positive for any of the cannabinoids in the scope of this method if the peaks in the sample correspond to the retention time of the peaks in the CCV injections and are above the LOQ. See Table 14.
Any unknown sample peaks greater than the lower limit of quantitation (LOQ), but less than the upper limit of quantitation (ULOQ; the highest standard point), must be reported.
Any unknown sample peaks greater than the ULOQ should be diluted with ACN and re-injected, such that they fall between the LOQ and ULOQ.
